From superpower rivalry to today

For more than forty years after 1945, the United States and the Soviet Union competed for influence around the world without fighting each other directly. That Cold War shaped American foreign policy, the economy, civil liberties and even schools. It ended with the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 and the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991. The decades since have brought new challenges: terrorism, war, a financial crisis, and fierce debate over the government's role.

In this unit you will read four presidents on America's role in the world, then finish the semester as a citizen, not only a historian: you will choose a current issue, trace its roots through the history we have studied, and propose an action.

Look back at our two threads one last time. Who has had to fight for the full rights of citizenship since 1877? And how has the government's role in the economy changed?

Key terms: Cold War, containment, superpower, arms race, military-industrial complex, deliberation, civic action.
title: Pay Any Price
